incident-bot: PagerDuty -> page fired: PD-3892 | tenant=NimbusCorp | cluster=dedicated-us-east-3 | symptom=reserved_queue_latency_p95 high (350ms > 200ms) | rule=reserved-pool-latency | link=https://pagerduty.example/incidents/PD-3892

pagerduty: Incident PD-3892 triggered and notified on-call. Priority: P1.

mike: ack'd. I'll take initial triage. looking at Console metrics now.

mike: nginx-ingress HAProxy? nope, this is internal reserved queue on the dedicated runtime. seeing queue length jump for tenant NimbusCorp.

kevin: @mike thanks. do we have recent deploys for that tenant? any config rollouts?
mike: no recent deploys in their reserved pool. last autoscale event ~ 10m before alert.

mike: running PromQL to verify: ```sum(rate(reserved_queue_latency_seconds_bucket{tenant="NimbusCorp"}[5m])) by (le)``` seeing clear shift in p95 bucket. quick sample: p95=360ms, p99=720ms, queue_len=118.

emma: tagging logs for NimbusCorp requests: `klog -f --tenant NimbusCorp --cluster dedicated-us-east-3` shows repeated "enqueue timeout" traces and frequent KV cache misses for long contexts.

oncall-rotations: Reminder - runbook link for reserved pool latency: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/reserved-pool-latency. Steps 1-3: check pool utilization, check IO wait on GPUs, consider bumping reserved pool or enabling burst capacity.

mike: checked GPU utilization: nodes at 45-60% GPU usage, but host IO wait elevated on 2 nodes (iowait ~ 35%). disk metrics show increased swap activity on node-dus3-a. suspect host-level contention causing degraded throughput.

kevin: if it's host IO, increasing pool size won't fix host contention. we should cordon the noisy node and reschedule tenant pods off it. migration might be the quickest mitigation.

mike: preparing cordon/drain: ```kubectl cordon node-dus3-a && kubectl drain node-dus3-a --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force``` will cause short additional scheduling pressure but should relieve IO. ETA ~ 2-3m to drain.

sveta: I'll watch the drain and health checks. @mike if throughput drops further, i'll flip the tenant to their fallback model variant to reduce per-request load.

pagerduty: PD-3892 acknowledged by mike at 1769904330.

mike: drain started. provisioning notes: we should avoid scaling down the reserved pool during this window. disabling autoscaler for tenant NimbusCorp for the next 15m.

emma: notified customer success (CS) and sent templated high-latency message to NimbusCorp: "we're investigating elevated latency on your dedicated pool; may see brief retries. We'll update in 15 minutes."

kevin: escalated to infra on-call (infra-pager): paging infra for potential host filesystem issues. @infra-team please triage node-dus3-a iowait spike.

infra-team: infra-ack. checking host dmesg and iostat. preliminary root cause looks like background backup job hitting /var/lib/model-cache. killing backup process; disabling scheduled job on that host.

mike: drain complete. rescheduling pods onto nodes-dus3-b/c. early metrics: p95 down to 210ms, queue_len down to 34. p99 still elevated but trending down.

sveta: switching to partially rolled fallback for heavy-context model for NimbusCorp to further reduce KV cache pressure. applied feature-flag: `tenant.NimbusCorp.fallback=partial`

mike: monitoring — p95 stable ~185-200ms now. no new PD pages in the last 4m.

pagerduty: PD-3892 status: acknowledged -> under investigation.

kevin: CS confirmed NimbusCorp got the message and is monitoring. they reported spike around 11:12 PST, appreciate quick response.

sveta: handing off to @kevin for follow-up and post-incident writeup. I'm on lunch rotation after 11:50, cc on the writeup if needed.

kevin: ack handoff. will run through RCA steps: capture host metrics, note backup cron job, capture drain timing, DR plan (enable scheduled node isolation in host maintenance windows), and recommend change: avoid running backup on model-cache hosts; add iops limits for backup jobs.

mike: adding short-term action: add alert to notify when host iowait > 25% on nodes in reserved pools. filing ticket: RED-INC-1456.

pagerduty: PD-3892 resolved by mike at 1769904545. Resolution summary: backup job causing host IO contention on node-dus3-a -> cordon & drain relieved pressure -> KV cache miss rate decreased -> latency returned to baseline. Follow-ups assigned (RED-INC-1456, infra remediation, CS customer note).

emma: posting incident closure note to #incidents and tagging CS + account team.

kevin: thanks everyone. postmortem owners: kevin (infra remediation), mike (runbook tweaks + alert), sveta (tenant fallback playbook). I'll draft and circulate in 24h.

incident-bot: Thread closed by pagerduty after resolution.
